events.title: Old St Peter's Basilica is dedicated, by tradition
events.description: According to church tradition, Pope Sylvester I dedicated Constantine's basilica over the site of St Peter's tomb on the Vatican Hill. It stood for some 1,200 years before being replaced by the present church.
events.html: According to church tradition, Pope Sylvester I dedicated Constantine's basilica over the site of St Peter's tomb on the Vatican Hill. It stood for some 1,200 years before being replaced by the present church.

events.title: William Tell shoots the apple, according to legend
events.description: Swiss tradition dates to this day William Tell's shot at an apple on his son's head in Altdorf, ordered by the Habsburg bailiff Gessler. Historians regard the tale as legend, but it became a symbol of Swiss liberty.

events.title: Caxton completes the first dated book printed in England
events.description: At Westminster, William Caxton finished printing The Dictes or Sayengis of the Philosophres, the first book printed in England to carry a date. Printing in English helped standardise the language.
events.html: At Westminster, William Caxton finished printing The Dictes or Sayengis of the Philosophres, the first book printed in England to carry a date. Printing in English helped standardise the language.

events.title: Pope Urban VIII consecrates the new St Peter's Basilica
events.description: Exactly 1,300 years after the traditional dedication of the first basilica, Urban VIII consecrated the new St Peter's. Its design involved Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno over 120 years.
events.html: Exactly 1,300 years after the traditional dedication of the first basilica, Urban VIII consecrated the new St Peter's. Its design involved Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno over 120 years.

events.title: Latvia proclaims its independence
events.description: The People's Council in Riga declared an independent Latvian state. After a war of independence it remained free until Soviet occupation in 1940, regaining independence in 1991.
